claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: In `src/sqllens/server.py` lines 232 to 245, one `except Exception` now covers three different things: reading `model_extra` off the request, checking the shape and key count, and copying the tree with `copy_bounded_json`. All three failures log the same fixed line, `"invalid or oversized request metadata; returning empty metadata"`, with no exception type and no `exc_info`. A client sending a 20 KiB payload and a library fault inside the server therefore look identical in the log. The handler directly above it, at lines 218 to 228, carries a comment saying that unexpected failures must be logged with `exc_info=True` so that a future change in the MCP SDK stays diagnosable; the new handler covers that same surface and drops that property. `tests/unit/test_metadata_bounds.py` lines 547 to 554 pin the swallowing behaviour: a `RuntimeError` raised by the accessor is reported as invalid caller metadata. Behaviour stays fail-closed, so nothing is wrong with the result — but if every dynamic row-level-security query starts returning empty metadata, there is no signal saying why. Logging the exception class, or counting which bound was exceeded, would not echo any caller content. (raised by 3/6 agents)
